hero.name: Min Kim
hero.tagline: Hired as a product planner, became the company's first engineer
hero.description: Designed, built and shipped a B2B SaaS across web, iOS and Android as the sole developer in an organization with no engineering team. Worked on payments, auth, security and NFC in production, and took over stalled outsourced apps to bring them in-house.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: From planning to engineering
about.description1: I joined as a product planner, but with no engineers on staff my specs never got built. Building them myself turned out to be faster, so I did — and after shipping the product I moved into an engineering role.
about.description2: I now own the entire web service and the native apps. Subscription billing, multi-tenant security, native NFC integration and LLM-based document search were all built and debugged in a production environment with real paying customers.
about.description3: There was no engineering process in place, so I introduced one as needed — version control, database migrations, architecture documentation and security audits.

timeline.why: No engineer to implement the specs I wrote
No way to roll changes back
Manual schema edits caused an incident
Hard to reason about my own older code

items.title: TrayStorage Connect
items.summary: A B2B document management SaaS paired with NFC-tagged physical storage trays. I handled architecture, development, deployment and operations end to end.
highlights: Built subscription billing and migrated payment providers twice with no downtime for existing subscribers
Enforced multi-tenant isolation at the database level (118 row-level security policies)
Natural-language document search on 18 LLM function-calling tools, migrated away from vector RAG
details: A self-directed security audit surfaced object-storage credentials in the frontend bundle; I moved uploads and downloads onto server-issued presigned URLs. A second pass showed the code fix was neutralised by a manual key rotation that had never happened — I verified that empirically rather than trusting the checklist.

Pricing constants had to be duplicated across the browser and Deno edge runtimes, so I locked them together with a contract test that parses the edge sources and compares them against the client constant. If the values drift, the test fails.

Subscription expiry was enforced in the UI but not in four data-layer functions, so expired subscriptions still passed quota checks. I reproduced each existing definition and added exactly one line to each.
Five-language localization, including the full terms of service and privacy policy, with revisions that switch over automatically on their effective date.
Seven classes of personal data (national ID, driver's licence, passport, card, two phone formats, email) are detected by regex in OCR output and masked on the source image.

items.title: Four native apps taken over and rebuilt
items.summary: Took over four apps that had been outsourced and then left unmaintained for roughly 22 months. They were listed on the stores, but the product's core NFC flow was entirely broken and Naver sign-in was impossible because the external API it called had been retired.
highlights: Secured all four takeover baselines — the pre-takeover code can be checked out and built to reproduce the original state

Restored the NFC flow — three independent causes (zero intent filters, a dependency on the discontinued Firebase Dynamic Links, NDEF records in the wrong order) traced and replaced with locally assembled deep links
Fixed Naver sign-in — replaced the retired XML endpoint with the current JSON API and surfaced silent failures through a callback
details: Cut iOS LSApplicationQueriesSchemes from 66 entries to 49. Apple only honours the first 50, and Chrome and Google Maps sat at positions 65 and 66 — canOpenURL had been returning false for them the whole time, with no visible symptom.

Modernised a 2022 toolchain: Alamofire 4→5, Firebase 8→10, Kingfisher 5→7, GoogleSignIn 6→7, Kakao SDK v2, Facebook SDK removed, deployment target 15. Major-version upgrades broke the call sites, which I rewrote.
Cleared a Google Play rejection by removing the READ_MEDIA_IMAGES permission entirely rather than rewording its rationale, switching to the system photo picker — 84 lines less code.

Fixed defects including a non-static inner class Gson could not deserialise (registering a popup notice broke the main screen for every user), five error codes that disagreed with the server, and three null-pointer crashes on social sign-up profiles.

Removed a first-launch gate that demanded five permissions including location with no explanation and blocked entry if declined. Permissions are now requested from onboarding after stating their purpose — the app never called a location API anywhere.

Inherited a structure where Korean and English shipped as duplicated projects. Measured duplication at 94.7% on Android and 83% on iOS: consolidatable via product flavors and Xcode targets, but deferred because all four apps were already listed and changing applicationId risks the update path.
items.storeNote: All four are live — every listing runs a build containing my work (iOS last updated May 2026)

items.title: Native wrapper rebuilt from scratch
items.summary: An outsourced native wrapper stalled because NFC was never implemented, and the source code was never handed over. I rebuilt it from requirements alone, with nothing to reference.
highlights: NFC is structurally impossible through a web view alone — it requires a hand-written native bridge
Wrote four custom Capacitor plugins (NFC, push, speech-to-text, downloads)
All code now owned in-house, removing the dependency on the vendor
details: On iOS, Core NFC is a native-only API unreachable from WKWebView; on Android, Web NFC is disabled by default inside a WebView. Wrapping the web app was never going to be enough on its own.
Tag detection runs through a three-tier intent filter: tags carrying the service URL (NDEF_DISCOVERED), NDEF-formatted tags (TECH_DISCOVERED), and a catch-all for unformatted tags (TAG_DISCOVERED).

Configured universal links and app links, and complied with App Store guideline 3.1.1 by hiding payment UI in iOS builds — the replacement copy also avoids naming an external storefront, which 3.1.3 prohibits.

personal.name: Desktop Pet World
personal.tagline: Two LLM pets and their real-time 3D world, living on the desktop all day
personal.summary: A fork of the open-source desktop-pet app super-agent-party, with an entirely new 3D world layered on top. The render pipeline was redesigned around Apple Silicon thermals as a hard ceiling, and I built my own performance, regression and balance harnesses. Its two pets are LLM-driven — per-pet memory and TTS — and can step out of the world to roam the desktop itself in transparent always-on-top windows.
highlights: **Two LLM-driven pets with their own memory** — a chick and a puppy chat through a per-pet brain with server-side sessions and TTS, keep daily diaries, cook for each other, and speak up on world events (auroras, rainbows)
**Desktop companion mode** — the same pets roam the desktop itself in per-pet transparent always-on-top windows with tight hitboxes and per-window chat, sharing one brain with the 3D world

**Render pipeline redesigned under a thermal budget** — removed a post-processing chain (GTAO, bloom) stacking ~19 fullscreen passes per frame, replaced with a single forward pass plus MSAA. Idle-aware frame tiering at 60/30/15fps

**Three self-built verification harnesses** — a headless smoke test with a draw-call ceiling assertion, an fps/CPU probe across idle states, and a Monte Carlo balance simulator running 400 virtual days
**Away-day simulation** — days you never connect are simulated from a date seed and written up as a diary entry from the pet's point of view, then folded into the world log

gallery.caption: The plaza — fountain, vendor booths, fruit trees. Props are merged per material instance down to a few meshes per group
The archipelago — islands are generated from a deterministic seed and streamed in and out by view distance
House interior — loft and stairs, lit by real cast shadows rather than a render trick
Submarine — underwater foraging. Fish species share an atlas texture: one draw call each
Biplane — the sky refreshes every 30s while the sun and moon travel their arc
Night drive — vehicles move at 3× walking speed; tree colour varies by season

personal.galleryNote: A few frames from the running app.
details: **Storage layer hardened after a real incident** — following data loss, the write path was rebuilt around atomic replace (tmp + fsync + rename), generational backups, corruption quarantine and a three-step recovery ladder.
**3D modelling** — both characters modelled in Blender; procedural textures and vertex-colour gradients mean no texture assets ship at all.
**74,411 lines of upstream features cut** — removed across five deliberate commits after the fork, with a safety tag beforehand and the keep/remove boundary recorded with reasons.
